problem: End-to-end RL/IL visual navigation policies entangle perception and control. Their latent features overfit to the training simulator's appearance and to the training task. As a result, they generalize poorly to unseen scenes, transfer badly to a new simulator (Sim2Sim, a proxy for Sim2Real), and must be relearned from scratch for new embodied tasks. Naive fine-tuning on small target data even degrades performance.
motivation: Sim2Real is unsafe and hard to reproduce, so transfer between simulators of different fidelity (synthetic IndoorEnv, MP3D and Gibson scans) is used as a controllable proxy with a similar 'reality gap'. The driving observation is that embodied visual tasks decompose naturally into two parts: (1) task-agnostic geometric perception (depth, normals, free space); (2) a task-specific policy. If each part has its own supervision, one can be adapted while the other stays fixed.
key_idea: Train a shared visual encoder only with auxiliary visual (depth, surface normals, RGB reconstruction) and motion (egomotion, next-feature prediction) losses, then train the policy on the frozen encoder with gradients stopped. Transfer then fine-tunes only the encoder for a new simulator, or only the policy for a new task.
insight: Forcing the representation to encode geometry, rather than whatever spurious correlations the policy gradient finds, gives better in-simulator generalization. On MP3D val, SplitNet BC,PPO reaches SPL 0.716 vs 0.521 for E2E BC,PPO; ImageNet pretraining does not help (0.450). The decoupling also tells you which weights to adapt: in Table 3, fine-tuning encoder+policy (V+P) on 1-10 target scenes overfits (IndoorEnv→MP3D with 10 scenes: SPL 0.400 vs 0.531 for V-only; MP3D→Gibson V+P 'Failure'), whereas encoder-only adaptation steadily improves. With just 10 target scenes, SplitNet matches or beats E2E trained on the whole target dataset. Auxiliary tasks were not formally ablated; the authors report anecdotally that depth and normal prediction mattered most.
method: Visual encoder F: a CNN (7x7 stride-4 conv then 3x3 convs with GroupNorm+ELU, max-pools, 256 channels, avg-pool, linear 4096→256) maps a 256x256 RGB frame to a feature φt.
Auxiliary visual decoders: bilinear-upsampling conv decoders predict depth (L1), surface normals (cosine loss) and RGB reconstruction (L1) from φt, using simulator ground truth.

Auxiliary motion decoders: egomotion prediction from (φt, φt-1) via cross-entropy over the 3 discrete actions, and next-feature prediction P(φt-1, at)→φt via cosine loss. All auxiliary losses are combined as a weighted sum to train the encoder first.

Policy decoder: a GRU (input = 256-d feature + 2-d goal vector + 3-d previous-action one-hot) with actor (3 actions) and critic heads, trained on a frozen encoder with gradients stopped. Training is either BC (student forcing, geodesic-optimal expert action) or BC followed by PPO using a geodesic-progress reward plus a time penalty.

Sim2Sim transfer: on 1 or 10 target-simulator scenes, all decoders (policy and auxiliary) are frozen and only the shared encoder is updated. Gradients flow through the frozen decoders, including the policy decoder, so that the adapted features stay compatible with the fixed policy.

Task2Task transfer: starting from the Point-Nav BC,PPO model, the encoder is frozen and only the policy decoder is retrained with PPO on the new reward. The new tasks are Exploration (number of newly visited 1 m cells) and Flee (geodesic distance from the start).

setting.backbone: custom CNN encoder (GroupNorm+ELU) + GRU actor-critic policy, trained from scratch (no ImageNet init for SplitNet)
setting.training_data: Self-generated Point-Nav episodes in Habitat: MP3D has 61 train scenes and 5,000,000 episodes; Gibson has 72 scenes and 4,932,479 episodes; IndoorEnv (a synthetic 3D dataset) has 990 scenes and 898,267 episodes. The auxiliary losses use simulator ground-truth depth and surface normals. Sim2Sim adaptation uses 1 or 10 target-simulator train scenes. Exploration and Flee reuse the Point-Nav start points.
setting.observation: monocular RGB (256x256) + goal vector (distance, angle to goal, updated every step) + previous-action one-hot; Exploration/Flee get no position/goal info
setting.action_space: discrete: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 10°; no STOP action
setting.privileged: Per-step GT goal vector (distance/angle, i.e. GPS+compass-like). The STOP action is removed (success is judged by final position within 0.2 m). GT depth and normals are used only for training and target adaptation, not at test time.

numbers_note: All metrics are printed as fractions (e.g. 0.716) and converted to 0-100 here. Evaluation uses the authors' own sampled PointNav episodes: RGB-only, 0.2 m success radius, no STOP action, trivially easy episodes filtered out. These are not the official Habitat PointNav episodes, so comparisons with other papers need care. The Table A1 val-scene/val-episode columns appear swapped in the extracted text. Task2Task results (Exploration, Flee on IndoorEnv) are given only as learning curves in Figure 7, with no tabulated SplitNet numbers; only the oracles' 33.5 and 19.5 are stated. Table 3 also reports V+P fine-tuning ablations: IndoorEnv→MP3D 0.435/0.586 (1 scene) and 0.400/0.552 (10 scenes); MP3D→Gibson 'Failure'.
results: On unseen scenes, SplitNet BC,PPO reaches SPL 0.560 / 0.716 / 0.701 on IndoorEnv / MP3D / Gibson. The best E2E baselines are E2E BC,PPO at 0.393 / 0.521 on the first two and ImageNet-pretrained E2E BC,PPO at 0.642 on Gibson; E2E BC,PPO still has slightly higher Gibson success (0.869 vs 0.855). In Sim2Sim transfer with 10 target scenes, SplitNet gets MP3D SPL 0.531 vs 0.401 for E2E Finetune, and Gibson SPL 0.727 vs 0.667. This matches or beats E2E trained on the entire target dataset (0.521 / 0.606). E2E Finetune with 1 target scene degrades below the source model ('Failure'). In Task2Task transfer from Point-Nav to Exploration and Flee, SplitNet's policy-only retraining learns faster and better than E2E from scratch, E2E finetune and blind agents (Figure 7).
limitations: Transfer is only Sim2Sim, with no real-robot experiments. Target adaptation relies on auxiliary losses (depth, normals), whose ground truth is readily available only in simulation.
Non-standard PointNav protocol: custom episodes, STOP action removed, RGB-only. Task2Task results are shown only as curves.
No systematic ablation of which auxiliary tasks matter (left to future work); performance depends on choosing suitable auxiliary tasks.
